title: Character work
hook: the Musar movement works on one character trait at a time

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was kavanah: the heart aimed at what the hands or lips are doing. Your line was kavanah.

Ask a friend who they'd like to become, and the list comes fast. More patient. More generous. Honest even when it costs something. Calmer in traffic. Kinder to their brother. Ask when they're starting, and the list goes quiet. Where would anyone begin with all that? A Jewish movement of teachers gave an answer so plain it can sound like a trick. Don't start with the list. Start with one line on it, and stay there a while.
screen: `A LIST OF WHO YOU'D LIKE TO BE.` → `WHERE WOULD ANYONE BEGIN?` → `ONE LINE ON THE LIST.`

segments.voice: The movement is called Musar. In the book of Proverbs, musar is a Hebrew word for instruction or correction. The King James gives the line: "My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother." Jewish teachers used the word for writing about character, and a rabbi named Israel Salanter made it the name of a movement. Its starting point: the traits of a person, in Hebrew middot, can be worked on like a skill. Not admired from far off. Practiced. Patience, order, humility, generosity, honesty, calm. A saying often attributed to Salanter puts the difficulty bluntly: it is easier to learn the whole Talmud than to change a single trait. So you don't try to change them all. You pick one, and watch it through the day, where it holds and where it slips. Some practitioners write a line about it each night. Some repeat a short phrase, often a line from a text, until it settles in. After a stretch, they move to the next trait. The movement stood on older Jewish wisdom. The Mishnah's Ethics of the Fathers asks who is mighty, and answers with Proverbs: "He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city." Musar treats that inner work as the hard part, and the small daily gain as the real one.
screen: `MUSAR: INSTRUCTION, CORRECTION.` · `TRAITS CAN BE PRACTICED.` · `ONE TRAIT AT A TIME.` · `RULING YOUR OWN SPIRIT.` · then, large: `HE THAT RULETH HIS SPIRIT.`

segments.voice: Let a short list pass slowly through your mind: patience, honesty, generosity, order, humility, calm. Don't choose the one you think you ought to; choose the one where yesterday went wrong, where you snapped, rushed, held back or covered something over, and name it in one plain word. If you pray, you can ask for help with it; if you don't, simply hold the word and let it sit with you.
Musar. Instruction, correction: a Jewish movement of character work, practicing one trait at a time. Today's word.
Your line: one trait. Not a new self by Friday, but a little more patience by the end of the month. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: People who practice Musar often choose one middah, a trait such as patience or humility, and attend to it for a period of time, with daily notes, study of Musar texts and short repeated phrases, sometimes in a small group.
